limits: Steady conduction screen; fixed k, perfect contact to outer M6 cylindrical envelope. Thread helix/root/contact resistance unresolved.

Air and magnets thermally omitted. Copper omitted in pool mode; included in leads mode. No feed advection, wire melting, latent heat, transient heat capacity, Joule heating, external convection or radiation.

Pool mode assumes isothermal liquid. Leads mode instead solves stationary liquid/steel/copper temperature with fixed cold outer copper planes; it omits Joule heat, external losses and feeding, and uses fixed liquid k even if temperatures indicate freezing. Neither is a complete operation model.
native_cases.method: Existing native GPU scalar finite-volume operator with conductivity k. Outer cylindrical heated barrel at +0.5 K; selected pool or outer copper-plane boundary at -0.5 K. No new CPU or GPU PDE implementation.

interpretation: Raised pool alone does not keep the thin outlet hot if outer copper planes are held cold. For250C heater and25/200/230C copper boundaries, minimum liquid temperatures are107/218/237C. Below227C values flag SnCu freezing; fixed liquid k is retained for this conduction diagnostic. Heat contacts thermally from the heater through an electrical insulator, rather than cold-clamping them near the tip.
limits: No pulse-average Joule heat, feeding, cooling gas, phase-dependent k or real contact thermal resistance. Imposed copper boundary temperatures are hypotheses, not measured cable or contact temperatures.
